problem: Offline policy learning results on machine-generated data do not necessarily predict performance on temporally correlated, variable-quality human demonstrations.
contribution: A systematic robomimic study and public learning resource spanning data source/quality, temporal models, observations, hyperparameters, model selection and dataset size.
algorithm: Compare established imitation and offlineRL learners under controlled data/observation variations; strong recurrentBC captures human temporal correlations, while several batchRLmethods struggle on human data despite performance on machine mixtures.
observations: Low-dimensional robot/object state and image observations, including wrist views; crop/randomization choices are varied explicitly.
actions: Task-specific robot control targets from machine policies or human teleoperation, with binary completion rewards forRLcomparisons.
embodiment_and_data: SimulatedLift,Can,Square,Transport andToolHang datasets from machine, proficient-human and multi-human sources. RealFranka datasets contain200trajectories each forLift,Can andToolHang.
experiments: Three-seed simulation studies compare quality mixtures, image/state settings, architecture, dataset fractions and checkpoint selection. Real experiments report the finalcheckpoint over30rollouts without real-world hyperparameter tuning.
baselines: BC,BC-RNN,BCQ,CQL,HBC andIRIS; methods with temporal structure are strong human-data baselines, so an intentionallyweak feedforwardBC would be insufficient.

quantitative_result.note: Simulation tables select maximum online checkpoint performance; this is different from final/validation-loss selection.

limitations: Choosing the best online-tested checkpoint is impractical for physical evaluation and risks reuse of evaluation evidence. Lower validation imitationloss can mis-rank real performance; data and wrist-view benefits are task-dependent.
hardware_adaptation: Use the study to design robust human-data splits, temporal baselines and teaching guidance. Keep failed trajectories for analysis/RL with truthful labels rather than treating all operator actions as expertBCtargets.
algorithm_detail: This is an empirical design study, not a newly named learner. Its paired success/failure diagnostic and multi-human quality subsets distinguish offlineRL limitations from mere lack of trajectory variety; temporalBC and imageaugmentation choices are meaningful comparison factors.
integration_contract: Preserve operator/session IDs, sourcequality, actual target actions and camera preprocessing. Fit normalization ontrain only. Maintain separate development checkpoint selection and a never-retuned sealedtest.
license_evidence: The primarypaper and public repository pointer were verified. No model/data/source license audit is asserted; projectsiteP016 is a duplicatepointer, not anotherpaper.
required_experiments: ACT and strong recurrentBC on matched demonstrations; session/object splits; camera/augmentation ablation; validation-loss versus development-outcome selection; retain every sealedattempt and report all failures.
difference_from_explorer: Dataset curation and a multi-human recordingGUI are prior engineering/scientific subjects. Explorer must substantiate its additional sourcecompatibility, transfer and retention mechanism independently.
